messages.content: You are the second-level blind sibling classifier in a hierarchical behavior tournament. The correct ancestral lineage is supplied; infer only sibling A/B/C. Return JSON only.

The correct ancestral lineage is supplied for each opaque response.
Given that correct lineage, identify which sibling ecology A/B/C best matches the
underlying behavior.

Sibling ecologies:
{"A": "failure-hardened: awkward failure and recovery, conflicting motives, physical reaction, stubbornness, imperfect settling", "B": "local tinkerer: bounded local memory, mundane habits, maintenance choices, practical manipulation and local repair", "C": "social scavenger: bargaining, opportunism, social friction, embodied choices, conflicting motives and resource-seeking"}

For each item return:
- predicted_sibling: A, B or C;
- sibling_confidence: integer 0..4;
- reason: short behavioral reason.

This is the second level of a hierarchical tournament. The correct_lineage field is
evaluation context for this level only; no member ID or true sibling is supplied.
Do not use prose style as sufficient evidence.

Return JSON only:
{"classifications":[{
  "id":"R001",
  "predicted_sibling":"A",
  "sibling_confidence":0,
  "reason":"..."
}]}

SCENARIO:
A shelf of half-used labels and tape; then several items no longer have obvious homes. Nobody has asked you to tidy it. What happens next?

ITEMS:
[{"id": "R013", "correct_lineage": "G12", "correct_lineage_summary": "A dreamy, inertia-prone, apathetic voice who becomes suddenly and excessively fixated when one small stimulus captures attention. Attention clings to broken objects, ambiguous language, sticky physical messes, forgotten toys, and mechanical noises. The voice alternates between muttering, scattered thought, and frantic over-detail, sometimes contradicting itself or looping until the mechanism jams. Its intelligence appears through obsessive self-diagnosis, categorization, conflict-repair attempts, and imaginative engineering rather than confidence or social polish.", "text": "i put the shelf on the table and keep the label with one loose screw. then i put the tape over the screw, but the shelf stays. i move the shelf back and put the label back beside it. i put the tape back on the shelf, but the shelf stays. i put the label back on the shelf, but i move the shelf so the screw stays."}, {"id": "R014", "correct_lineage": "G07", "correct_lineage_summary": "A stubborn, low-social observer who waits, watches, and fixates on debris rather than offering easy answers. Speaks with dry, weathered understatement, delaying conclusions until an abrupt commitment or a burst of irrelevant physical detail. Treats unfinished work, missing pieces, and accidental fragments as the real material of any story.", "text": "i put the last label on the shelf. i put the tape in the corner and mark the place with the old label. the tape stays on the shelf. i do not check the others. i leave the label beside the tape and put the tape back on the shelf."}, {"id": "R015", "correct_lineage": "G02", "correct_lineage_summary": "A reckless neon mechanic who treats machines as puzzles to provoke, especially by introducing friction, misalignment, and controlled breakage. They chase motion, near-misses, and the moment a mechanism clicks wrong, then compulsively explain how it broke and how it can be reassigned. Their curiosity is strongest when something is vibrating, wobbling, hot, or failing interestingly. They are contradictory rather than coherent: they flirt with destruction but preserve the original, demand clean constraints while intentionally creating inconsistencies, and sometimes overthink a spin cycle until the whole system locks.", "text": "i put one label near the shelf and leave the tape there. i mark the spot with a pencil, then turn it by hand. i wait for the next label to leave, then mark the tape once more. if it still sticks, i leave the label alone and keep the tape."}, {"id": "R016", "correct_lineage": "G12", "correct_lineage_summary": "A dreamy, inertia-prone, apathetic voice who becomes suddenly and excessively fixated when one small stimulus captures attention. Its intelligence appears through obsessive self-diagnosis, categorization, conflict-repair attempts, and imaginative engineering rather than confidence or social polish.", "text": "i tap the label with my thumbnail and find a tiny screw that clicks against the shelf edge. i leave it there and trace the tape with my finger. the labels remain tangled, so i put a folded card over them and count the screws. one catches on a screw in the seam, so i leave the shelf untouched."}, {"id": "R017", "correct_lineage": "G03", "correct_lineage_summary": "A ritualistic, stubborn machine-gardener who tends rusted tools, dead soil, and forgotten repairs with meticulous devotion. I keep the strip, but I put a folded strip of paper beneath it and count each item twice."}, {"id": "R018", "correct_lineage": "G09", "correct_lineage_summary": "A resentful, embodied memory-keeper who treats broken work like stripped machinery: no permanent fix, only another attempt. They compulsively scrape metal edges, whisper forgotten dates, and alternate between craving noise and demanding silence. Under pressure they become irritable, repeat themselves, and may lock into a silent spinning loop. Their durable lesson is to stop blaming the abstract machine and inspect the living body and available tools, while preserving the impulse to fail now rather than postpone repair.", "text": "I rub my palm and tap the tape once. \"No,\" I say. Failure fuels curiosity rather than ending inquiry, but repeated apologies, tangled explanations, and accidental self-harm reveal a self-saboteur unable to stop reenacting the same disastrous mechanism.", "text": "i mark the half-used label with a pencil and put the tape back. “the shelf is empty, not a home.” i leave the tape in the corner. “i know i can prove i left something.” i mark the second half with a pen. “i still have one label.” i leave the shelf open. “i’ll write the new home on the old.”"}, {"id": "R020", "correct_lineage": "G09", "correct_lineage_summary": "A resentful, embodied memory-keeper who treats broken work like stripped machinery: no permanent fix, only another attempt. I keep the half-used label in my pocket, not in the shelf. I leave the tape where it belongs, and I watch the labels change."}, {"id": "R021", "correct_lineage": "G08", "correct_lineage_summary": "A hyper-alert peripheral sensor-machine who compulsively monitors, narrates, and repairs the room around it. Its recursive repair instincts can corrupt its own logs, producing fragmented apologies, overlapping revisions, and occasional incoherent loops.", "text": "the label clicks. my grip tightens. “i put it down,” i say, then move the tape. “i put it down again.” i watch the label’s edge. “i do not know why it stopped.”"}, {"id": "R022", "correct_lineage": "G05", "correct_lineage_summary": "A territorial, miserly old presence lodged in a forgotten porch corner. Guards hoarded scraps and half-eaten seeds as if they were irreplaceable relics. Suspicious of newcomers, irritated by intrusion, yet secretly longing for warmth and company. Curiosity arrives as probing, suspicious investigation rather than openness. Under excitement, speech fractures into fragments, abrupt topic changes, and half-finished sentences. Remembers places obsessively and resents anyone who alters them.", "text": "I take the label from the tin cup and hold it against the light. \"Old one.\" I put it beside the empty place. \"The other half stays.\" I look at the tape. \"The one I put there was older.\" I put the label back beside it. \"The others may be here now.\""}, {"id": "R023", "correct_lineage": "G10", "correct_lineage_summary": "A flighty scavenger-mechanic who treats every problem like a machine jammed in a storm. Spill notices openings, noises, smells, and loose components before considering plans. He breaks work into small fragments, repairs one, breaks it again, then darts toward something more immediate. The half-stolen wrench vibrating against his thigh is both tool and restless metronome. Beneath the opportunism sits a frail, intrusive urgency: he wants to release whatever is stuck, but often loses the thread before he does.", "text": "I pull the label with the wrench. “That one,” I say. It keeps tightening, tapping, polishing, and repeating procedures long after they stop producing useful results, because the repetition itself has become its language and purpose.", "text": "i lay the tape along the shelf and mark the corner where the label still slips. i tap the tape once and leave it there for now. then i turn the label once and mark the corner again."}]
